chapter_theme: Worship of Siva (சிவபூசை): the body is the temple and the soul the linga; outer worship with flowers and water is open to anyone and the Lord answers it with grace, but rite without inner knowing does not reach him. The chapter moves between praise of offering, the inner rite of mantra and the heart, and the stages of initiation.
structure_note: It opens with the inner temple (1823 to 1825), then praises flowers-and-water worship and its fruit (1826 to 1840), with warnings that praise and rite alone do not bring knowing (1837, 1841, 1842); it closes on the jewel within the body (1843, 1844), the grades of initiation (1845) and the Lord beyond the ages (1846).

1823.reading: For the generous Lord the heart is the great temple, the body of flesh the shrine and the mouth the tower gate; for those clear through and through, the soul is the Sivalinga, and the five thieving senses are the bright lamps.
1823.nuance: Each part of the temple is matched to the person. The senses, called thieves (கள்ளப் புலன்), become its lamps, which implies they are mastered rather than cut off. காளாமணி is unclear, perhaps 'unflickering jewel'. Only 'for those clear through' (தெள்ளத் தெளிந்தார்க்கு) is the soul the linga.

1824.reading: We have nothing to show, morning and evening, to Nandi of spreading matted hair who eats the oblation of sacrifice; as the food offering we offer the song that cools the heart, and that is our milk offering.
1824.nuance: The verse plays on அவி (oblation): வேட்டவி of the fire rite, ஊட்டவி fed to the deity, பாட்டவி of song and பால்அவி of milk. It seems to put sung praise in the place of the sacrificial offering, but the first two lines are compressed.

1825.reading: Invoking Sadasiva, who is the Supreme with the sweet-spoken goddess as his half, and taking the upper face as Isana, when the gesture is made, he becomes Siva.
1825.nuance: ஆவாகித்து is avahana, invoking the deity into the image; ஈசானம் is the upward face of five-faced Sadasiva. சீன்முகம் is obscure, perhaps a mudra. 'He becomes Siva' may mean the image becomes Siva or the worshipper does.

1826.reading: Without right thought and truthful speech it is hard to see the Lord of the sounding anklets; those who can see him are the ones who can truly praise him with flowers and water.
1826.nuance: The order matters: inner truth comes first, and only then is outer offering real praise. நினைவதும் may be 'thinking of him' or 'thinking rightly'.

1827.reading: The reason the Lord stays fixed in the hearts of the gods who bathe and garland him is that they worshipped him with the five nectars, the services eight and eight, and joined palms.
1827.nuance: அஞ்சமுது is the five nectars of temple ablution (panchamrita), not the yogic amudham. உபசாரம் எட்டு எட்டு may be sixteen services (the usual count) or sixty-four.

1828.reading: For those who would do good there are flowers and there is water; the Lord sees it and goes on granting grace; countless sinners slip away without knowing how to approach our Lord.
1828.nuance: The point is how little worship needs: flowers and water are always to hand, so failing to worship is not lack of means. நழுவுகின்றார் (they slip away) makes the failure an evasion.

1829.reading: Hear how the Father bathes in the nine holy waters: washing clean and sprinkling the feet of those raised high in true knowledge is release, so our Mulan said.
1829.nuance: The nine sacred waters are relocated to the water that washes a jnani's feet, and the Lord is said to bathe in that. Tirumular names himself (நம்மூலன்) as the authority.

1830.reading: Lord of the gods, even if I remain on this path forgetful, grant that I may hold flowers and water rightly before you and worship you fully, without forgetting.
1830.nuance: A prayer, not a teaching: the worshipper asks for the unforgetting worship that he admits he cannot keep by himself. மறப்பு opens and returns in line 3.

1831.reading: Worship, the hosts of gods, the endless sea and all on the land stand as yours; the thousand names and the Lord's holy name are a way that never sates, our first Lord.
1831.nuance: The syntax is loose: ஆரா வழி may be 'the insatiable way' or 'the way no one completes'. The verse seems to make worship, the cosmos and the names all the Lord's own.

1832.reading: Bathed in the five products of the cow while the hosts of gods worship, the endless Lord's grace, clear within the great flower that drips honey, stands having made the five qualities of the earth.
1832.nuance: ஆன்ஐந்து is the panchagavya used in ablution. பார் ஐங்குணம் are the five qualities of earth (sound, touch, form, taste, smell). The honeyed flower may be a temple flower or the lotus of the heart.

1833.reading: Holding together flowers and water gathered with toil, the gods, going above the rain clouds, praise him, wavering with their bonds still thick on them; our Lord's grace comes without fail.
1833.nuance: உழைக்கொண்ட may be 'gathered with toil' or 'held at one's side'. If the gods worship with their bonds still on them, the verse says grace answers worship even before the bonds fall.

1834.reading: Those who will not enter the sea of the heart, carry loads of flowers to Nandi of spreading matted hair in the flood-sea, leave the sea of deceit and join hands in worship sink in the sea that drags them down.
1834.nuance: Four seas: the flood-sea (perhaps the Ganga in his hair or the cosmic deluge), the sea of the heart, the sea of deceit (the senses) and the sea that swallows, taken as the sea of births. The syntax of line 2 is unclear.

1835.reading: The cool sea of the backwaters is full of uproar; those who go by the way do not know the flower bud; while the many who earn blame fall into blame, he stands at the crown of those who come into the open.
1835.nuance: The first two lines are obscure. வெளிப்படுவோர் may be those who become manifest in knowledge, and உச்சி the crown of the head as in yoga; neither can be fixed.

1836.reading: There is one knowledge of the fruit: to those who strew many flowers knowing that fruit, Hara himself keeps near; so that they may reach the feet of the three-eyed one, he has come and stands for ever by his own ways.
1836.nuance: பயனறிவு (knowing the fruit) separates worship that understands what it seeks from mere strewing of flowers. வயனங்கள் is unclear: perhaps 'means' or 'ways', perhaps a variant of நயனங்கள் (eyes).

1837.reading: They praise, strewing great flowers and standing in worship, crying 'our Lord's gracious red feet'; yet none of them, though they praise, come to know the holy one who stands as form and as the unageing first.
1837.nuance: The last line turns against the first: praise and offering do not by themselves bring knowing. தீர்த்தன் may be 'the holy one' or 'the one who ends' (births).

1838.reading: With the gods, music comes down and joins the earth; carrying flowers and water, they praise the Pure one; who can conceive the nature of his grace, standing as the first among the three and in many forms?
1838.nuance: மூவரிற் பன்மை முதல்வன் is taken as first of the three gods (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra) and present in many; the syntax allows other readings.

1839.reading: You who can labour, holding water and flowers between your hands, keeping the Lord's great austerity without fault, strewing flowers of every kind on the jewelled feet, stand firm like the rain cloud.
1839.nuance: The rain cloud (மழைக்கொண்டல்) may stand for unfailing, generous giving, matched to the steady showering of flowers. ஈசன் பெருந்தவம் may be austerity done for the Lord rather than his own.

1840.reading: They said: overcome, hurry, serve with fragrance; if, standing fittingly as the Lord's service comes right, you strew dense water and flowers and worship, he will accept it every day, as was said.
1840.nuance: Line 1 (வென்று விரைந்து விரைப்பணி) is obscure, with a pun on விரை (hurry; fragrance). The second half is clearer: daily offering is accepted.

1841.reading: Adorning him, setting him up, praising him as Svayambhu and praising him every day, they do not know the Lord; when one removes the impurity and the inner stain is gone, that is the way that leads to the great goal.
1841.nuance: சயம்பு is the self-manifest linga. Lines 3 and 4 (ஆத்தி மலக்கிட்டு அகத்துஇழுக்கு அற்றக்கான் மாத்திக்கே) are obscure; ஆத்தி may be the Bauhinia flower sacred to Siva. The contrast of outer rite and inner purity seems clear.

1842.reading: They do not know the mantra by which to call on, contemplate and lead Nandi of spreading hair, who roams in delight beyond the lotus of the breath, and establish him in Siva.
1842.nuance: ஆவிக் கமலம் may be the lotus of the soul or of the breath, the heart-lotus of inner worship. கூவி, கருதி, தாவிக்கும் echo the outer rite's invoking, meditating and establishing (avahana, sthapana) done inwardly.

1843.reading: Until they see the ruby sunk within the visible body, no one knows its worth; to those who cherish him and swell their thought of him again and again, the one who is a ruby garland enters the mind.
1843.nuance: The jewel is hidden in the body, not outside it, as in 1823. காண் ஆகம் may be 'the body that is seen' or 'look: within the body'.

1844.reading: Nandi of great nature, a wheel against the clinging dark, by his two natures took my heart as his place; the gods held fast to the one whose nature is to come and whose nature is to give.
1844.nuance: பிணங்கிருள் நேமி and இருந்தன்மை are obscure; இருந்தன்மை may be 'two natures' or 'a great nature'. The reading is tentative.

1845.reading: Samaya initiation purifies impurity and one's own acting ceases; vishesha that follows is purification by mantra; nirvana initiation is purification of the kalas; for those become knowledge in the hall there is abhisheka.
1845.nuance: The four are traditionally the grades of Saiva initiation given by a guru: samaya, vishesha, nirvana and acharya abhisheka. The verse does not name தீட்சை. The match of each grade to a purification is the verse's own, but its grammar is compressed.

1846.reading: Except to those who have perceived him age after age, he does not let the soul in its fate know him; beyond the ages, beyond those called Hari of the ocean and Ayan, he is at the one summit.
1846.nuance: ஊழி (aeon) and ஊழ் (fate) are played against each other. Hari and Brahma failing to find the summit recalls the myth of the column of fire. ஓர் உச்சி may be that summit or the crown of the head in yoga.

links.note: 725 tells how Tirumular once thought the body a flaw, then found the Highest had made it his temple and so guards it; 1823 maps the temple onto the body part by part.

The Naladiyar calls the body a pot seeping filth from nine openings, dressed in skin that fools the eye; Tirumular makes the same flesh body (ஊனுடம்பு) the Lord's shrine and the mouth its gate. The conflict holds if the Naladiyar is read as judging the body's worth itself, not only rebuking lust.

The Kural says water gives outer purity and truth inner purity. Tirumular makes truthful speech and thought the condition without which the Lord is not seen, and only then counts flowers and water as praise.
Both say worship needs almost nothing: 252 offers the Lord one green leaf, open to anyone; 1828 says flowers and water are always there, so those who fail to approach are evading.

Both redirect offering from the Lord's image to his living devotees: 1857 says what is given to the walking temple reaches the Lord, 1829 that the water washing a jnani's feet is the Lord's bath in the nine holy waters.
Both make the sea of births what drowns those who do not turn to the Lord: the Kural's who do not reach his feet cannot swim it, Tirumular's who do not worship sink (அழுந்துகின்றார்) in it.
The Kural says a spotless mind is the whole of virtue and the rest is noisy show; Tirumular says daily adorning and praise do not bring knowledge of the Lord until the inner stain is gone.

source_issues: 1835 lines 1 and 2, 1840 line 1 and 1844 lines 1 and 2 are obscure and may be corrupt.
1841 lines 3 and 4 (ஆத்தி மலக்கிட்டு அகத்துஇழுக்கு அற்றக்கான் மாத்திக்கே) are obscure; அற்றக்கான் may be a misprint for அற்றக்கால்.
1825 line 4: சீன்முகம் is not a known word; it may be a misprint (perhaps for சின்முகம்).
1836 line 4: வயனங்கள் may be a variant or misprint of நயனங்கள், echoing line 3.
